deeper_properties: Powers of a fixed complex number rotate by a fixed angle: the argument of $(1+i\sqrt{3})^n$ advances by $60°$ per step, so the sign of the real part cycles with period 6 in $n$.
A sign alternating over even indices is $(-1)^k = i^{2k}$: alternation on the $k$-th term is the fingerprint of an imaginary base.
The odd-index terms of the expansion carry the $i$; taking the real part is what deletes them, which is why only even indices appear.

candidates.name: Real part of (1 + i√3)^{2020} by de Moivre
candidates.from_first_principles: The general term $(-3)^k \binom{2020}{2k}$ is $\binom{2020}{2k} (i\sqrt{3})^{2k}$, exactly the even-index terms of $(1+i\sqrt{3})^{2020}$, so the sum is its real part. In polar form $1+i\sqrt{3} = 2e^{i\pi/3}$, so the real part is $2^{2020}\cos(2020\pi/3) = 2^{2020} \cdot (-\tfrac12) = -2^{2019}$.
